java.say: c() still belongs to A. It now asks B to do the work.
This is the only call from A to B. A still has one dependency on B, as before.
It prints B's own field j. B needs no getter anymore, and A needs to know less about B.
A keeps only its own data. Both classes keep their data and the work on it together: cohesion went up.
